Typically, the ex-dividend date is one business day before the record date, which is the date on which a company determines the shareholders eligible to receive a dividend. It is important to be aware of the ex-dividend date because any trade on the stock needs to have been settled on or before the record date. Meaning, you will need to purchase ResMed's shares before the 12th of November to receive the dividend, which will be paid on the 17th of December.

The company's next dividend payment will be US$0.66 per share, and in the last 12 months, the company paid a total of US$2.64 per share. If you buy this business for its dividend, you should have an idea of whether ResMed's dividend is reliable and sustainable. So we need to investigate whether ResMed can afford its dividend, and if the dividend could grow.

We've found 21 US stocks that are forecast to pay a dividend yield of over 6% next year. See the full list for free.

Dividends are typically paid from company earnings. If a company pays more in dividends than it earned in profit, then the dividend could be unsustainable. ResMed has a low and conservative payout ratio of just 22% of its income after tax. That said, even highly profitable companies sometimes might not generate enough cash to pay the dividend, which is why we should always check if the dividend is covered by cash flow. The good news is it paid out just 22% of its free cash flow in the last year.

It's encouraging to see that the dividend is covered by both profit and cash flow. This generally suggests the dividend is sustainable, as long as earnings don't drop precipitously.

Businesses with strong growth prospects usually make the best dividend payers, because it's easier to grow dividends when earnings per share are improving. Investors love dividends, so if earnings fall and the dividend is reduced, expect a stock to be sold off heavily at the same time. That's why it's comforting to see ResMed's earnings have been skyrocketing, up 28% per annum for the past five years. ResMed looks like a real growth company, with earnings per share growing at a cracking pace and the company reinvesting most of its profits in the business.

Since the start of our data, 10 years ago, ResMed has lifted its dividend by approximately 8.2% a year on average. It's encouraging to see the company lifting dividends while earnings are growing, suggesting at least some corporate interest in rewarding shareholders.

Final Takeaway

From a dividend perspective, should investors buy or avoid ResMed? ResMed has been growing earnings at a rapid rate, and has a conservatively low payout ratio, implying that it is reinvesting heavily in its business; a sterling combination. data.description:

ManpowerGroup Investment Narrative Recap

To own ManpowerGroup, you need to believe its AI tools, Experis and Talent Solutions can steadily lift margins in a business that has seen flat longer term revenue and weaker earnings per share. The short term swing factor is how quickly the multi year US$200m cost program and AI platforms translate into cleaner EBITA margin progress.

The biggest risk remains pressure on gross profit, especially in staffing where mix and prior divestments already weigh, and where any further squeeze could offset efficiency gains. The Fonseca appointment looks directionally helpful for execution on AI and process work, but on its own it does not materially change near term risks.

The Fonseca board election ties most clearly to ManpowerGroup’s push around PowerSuite, Sophie AI and an AI driven sales engine that is already linked with about US$200m of incremental revenue. Her Pfizer track record in scaling enterprise AI and process excellence fits into the same operational problem set, from workflow automation to better sales targeting.

For investors, the question is whether that additional expertise improves the likelihood that AI and the US$200m cost program deliver the intended EBITA margin lift while avoiding fresh disruption. Execution still has to contend with staffing margin pressure, sensitive free cash flow and debt that is not well covered by operating cash flow.

What The Consensus Numbers Assume For ManpowerGroup

Analysts sketch a fairly specific arc for ManpowerGroup over the next few years, and it is worth testing whether that story feels realistic to you as a shareholder or potential investor. The projections lean heavily on AI driven productivity, a leaner cost base and a richer mix of higher value services, all of which the Fonseca appointment is meant to sharpen.

Revenue assumptions are clear. Forecasts build in 3.7% yearly top line growth over the next three years, which, if sustained out to 2029, feeds into projected sales of US$21.1b. That rate of expansion sits on top of a staffing and workforce solutions platform that has historically been more cyclical and volume driven, so the bet is that ManpowerGroup can rely more on differentiated services and AI supported offerings to support that pace.

Profitability expectations are even more explicit. Consensus modeling moves profit margins from 0.6% today to 1.8% in three years, effectively tripling margin on each dollar of revenue. That uplift leans on the planned US$200m cost savings program, the scaling of platforms like PowerSuite and Sophie AI, and a mix tilt toward Experis and Talent Solutions that is meant to carry richer economics than traditional staffing.

Earnings forecasts sit at the center of this. Analysts expect earnings to reach US$374.9m by around 2029, up from US$120.3m today, with the more cautious views closer to US$335.3m. That implies earnings a little over 3x current levels, which is a sizeable reset in profit power given the recent history of weaker earnings per share and softer return on invested capital.

To support the analyst price targets, the stock would need to trade on a P/E of 8.8x those forecast earnings, down from 17.3x today and also below the current 23.4x for the wider US Professional Services group. That setup suggests the scenario is not only about earnings growth but also about the market being willing to value ManpowerGroup on a lower multiple than sector peers in 2029.

ManpowerGroup's narrative projects US$21.1b revenue and US$374.9m earnings by 2029. This requires 3.7% yearly revenue growth and an earnings increase of about US$254.6m from US$120.3m today.

The equity story also leans on a discount rate of 8.78%, in line with the Simply Wall St company report, to translate those future cash flows into today’s valuation anchor.

Consensus sits at US$52.33, around 14.7% above the current US$44.64 share price, with a bullish camp up at US$65.00 and a cautious group closer to US$47.00.
